title: An EC2NodeClass with no capacityReservationSelectorTerms stops using open ODCRs
quote: If you use ODCRs with `open` instance eligibility but have **not** set `spec.capacityReservationSelectorTerms` on your EC2NodeClasses, Karpenter stops using those reservations after this upgrade and falls back to on-demand — leaving reservations unused but still billed. Configure it **before** upgrading; see the native ODCR support guide.
remediation: Set `spec.capacityReservationSelectorTerms` on these node classes BEFORE upgrading if you use On-Demand Capacity Reservations with `open` instance eligibility. Native ODCR support turns on by default at 1.6, and a node class that does not name its reservations stops using them and falls back to on-demand — the reservations keep billing while nothing runs on them.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ec2nodeclasses -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | select(.spec.capacityReservationSelectorTerms == null) | .metadata.name'  # each node class printed stops using open ODCRs, which stay billed but idle
coversNotes: Native ODCR support has graduated to beta and is enabled by default.
